title: Introduce UnitSmith: auto-calibrate conservative batching, cache and quant defaults
author: Aisha Kaur
description: Motivation: Operators repeatedly ask for safe, conservative defaults for batching, prefix caching and quantization that reduce unit cost without risking regressions in tail latency or quality. This PR adds UnitSmith, a small policy engine that auto-calibrates tenant-level defaults based on historical traffic shapes and an internal safety model. High-level changes: 1) policy engine (services/econ/autocalibrator) that ingests sampling histograms and emits recommended profiles; 2) a conservative profile template set for batch_size, prefill_kv_cache, and quant_profile; 3) CLI and rwctl integration to preview and apply recommendations; 4) telemetry hooks and eval gating to avoid applying profiles that increase eval regression metrics. Related work: design doc https://redwood.internal/docs/unitsmith-design (ENG-3427), prior prefilling work ENG-174999. Checklist: - [x] core autoscaler properly respects tenant SLAs - [x] unit tests for policy decision logic - [x] end-to-end smoke with synthetic traffic - [x] doc entry and operator runbook - [x] CI green and e2e flake < 1% Rollout plan: feature gate behind flags.autocalibrate: disabled by default; dry-run mode in rwctl; canary rollout to 10 tenants this week, monitor cost/latency deltas for 48h; automatic rollback on latency spike > 15 p90 or quality regression measured by eval harness in CI. How it works (brief): UnitSmith consumes the workload profiler snapshots and a tenant risk score to pick a target profile from the conservative template family. It simulates expected token throughput and runs a lightweight micro-sim that models KV cache hit rate changes and token-per-inference cost to estimate unit economics and expected latency tail. Safety gates include: a quality delta threshold, a latency tail threshold, and a per-tenant minimal headroom setting. Backwards compatibility: profiles are additive and optional; existing tenant configs are not mutated unless rwctl apply --auto is used. Migration: no DB schema changes. Operator docs and API contract in docs/unitsmith.md. Testing notes: e2e harness can be run with ./hack/e2e.sh --unitsmith-canary to reproduce the canary flow. Metrics and dashboards included in dashboards/unit_smith_overview.json. Security: no new privileges; uses existing tenant-scoped role to write recommended profiles. Rollback: rwctl revert-profile <tenant> restores pinned profile. Why conservative? We intentionally bias toward lower-cost wins with higher safety margins in this first iteration. Future work: tighter quant-profile search, tenant grouping heuristics, and automated canary expansion.
